FROMLIST: drm/mediatek: add background color input select function for ovl/ovl_2l This patch add background color input select function for ovl/ovl_2l ovl include 4 DRAM layer and 1 background color layer ovl_2l include 4 DRAM layer and 1 background color layer DRAM layer frame buffer data from render hardware, GPU for example. backgournd color layer is embed in ovl/ovl_2l, we can only set it color, but not support DRAM frame buffer. for ovl0->ovl0_2l direct link usecase, we need set ovl0_2l background color intput select from ovl0 if render send DRAM buffer layer number <=4, all these layer read by ovl. layer0 is at the bottom of all layers. layer3 is at the top of all layers. if render send DRAM buffer layer numbfer >=4 && <=6 ovl0 read layer0~3 ovl0_2l read layer4~5 layer5 is at the top ot all these layers. the decision of how to setting ovl0/ovl0_2l read these layer data is controlled in mtk crtc, which will be another patch Signed-off-by: Yongqiang Niu <yongqiang.niu@mediatek.com> (am from https://patchwork.kernel.org/patch/10872703/) BUG=b:126008314 TEST=Boot to shell Signed-off-by: CK Hu <ck.hu@mediatek.com> Change-Id: Ibedea2f1642cbf7a17605aa49c3b8b6735e2d0fc Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1361008 Commit-Ready: CK Hu <ck.hu@mediatek.corp-partner.google.com> Tested-by: CK Hu <ck.hu@mediatek.corp-partner.google.com> Reviewed-by: Sean Paul <seanpaul@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: CK Hu <ck.hu@mediatek.corp-partner.google.com> Reviewed-by: Nicolas Boichat <drinkcat@chromium.org>

device_data: move constants to a separate module device_data module provides functions to access stored device data (on factory state server), which has many dependencies, e.g. 'jsonrpclib'. However, some modules only import device_data because they need to reference to the constants defined in device_data module. These modules should not depend on jsonrpclib. configless_fields is an example, it imports device_data module because it needs the constants defined in the module, itself won't access factory state server directly. This CL moves these constants to a separate module so we don't introduce extra dependencies. power: refactor RTC wakealarm usage model Backdrop: We used to have many false positive cases in partners' engineering that the native suspend_stress_script been interrupted due to an early wakeup of wakealarm. With regard to the Chrome-OS power manager, we have some special power manager test clients in native and remote which are designed to validate no kernel/firmware issue during suspend path. These clients are basically composed by the RTC wakealarm as the engine to perform test iterations, typically these clients are not used by the end users. Now there is a problem in between test clients and power manager daemon: - The test clients program RTC wakealarm before issuing suspend request through the dbus to the daemon - The power manager daemon has internal suspender delay policy allows registered applications to be ready for system suspending Consider the interface is dbus, the above two are conflict because they do not know each other in terms of encapsulation: - The test client would not know the daemon has delay policy while it programmed wakealarm first, i.e, suspender is opaque to test client - The power daemon policy instance has no idea w.r.t wakealarm budget it should follow-up, nor it has permission to access the RTC Solution: This patch refactors the RTC wakealarm assignment from before the suspender to after it. Such that, the suspender delay policy will not conflict w/ pre-programming the wakealarm. Also the wakealarm timeout would approach the time we expect that the machine should stay in a low power state. In short explanation, it defers the wakealarm programming from the test client to the powerd setuid helper script. Note: There is limitation for manual issuing the powerd_dbus_suspend w/ wakeup_timout, it requires a correct wakeup_count option as well. BUG=chromium:941846, b:112335777, b:113242596, b:123243506, b:73018133 TEST=run the 'suspend_stress_test' w/ or w/o --memory_check option, run the 'powerd_dbus_suspend' w/ or w/o wakeup_timeout respectively, examime the footprints in powerd log and syslog to justify the wakealarm usage against the Suspender. Change-Id: I0fa3e11162ab8ca5565a342cdd7b098ee04e6947 Signed-off-by: Harry Pan <harry.pan@intel.com> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1517064 Reviewed-by: Dan Erat <derat@chromium.org>

factory_bootstrap: disable journald to speed up boot time systemd-journald is not available in initramfs, therefore /etc/init/journald.conf would always fail. The init script would wait for 60 seconds to confirm a socket is not created. Just like we don't need syslog, we don't really need journald in initramfs. This CL disable journald.conf.
